highlights:
# Modal drops H100 GPU pricing to $3.95/hour 💰 | AI Infrastructure News · LinkedIn · 2026-11-03T00:00:00+00:00

**AI Infrastructure News**.

---

Modal drops H100 GPU pricing to $3.95/hour 💰

That's 15-20% below most cloud providers. And it's happening while Akamai ships B300 GPUs on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra systems.

The GPU cloud market just got more competitive. Here's what 6 providers are charging as of October 2026:

• Modal: $3.95/hour for H100
• Akamai: B300 GPU on HGX B300 systems (announced Oct 27)
• 4 other providers with varying H100 rates

Modal's pricing undercuts the median by a significant margin. They're betting on volume over margin.

Akamai's play is different. They're racing to get Blackwell Ultra GPUs into production. The B300 gives them architectural advantages over H100-based infrastructure.

results.title: Modal Labs Pricing 2026: GPU Rates, Plans and Credits
results.author: Dario Espinoza-Blum
highlights:
Summary

Modal charges per second for compute with no flat fee on the Starter plan, making costs depend largely on GPU choice, how long code runs and whether containers sit idle waiting. An H100 GPU kept running for a full day costs $94.80, but Modal does not charge for idle resources.

- T4 GPU costs $0.59 hourly; H100 costs $3.95 hourly.
- Per-second billing charges 40 seconds for a 40-second task; per-minute charges 60.

...

At $0.59 an hour, a T4 suits light jobs, according to gpu.blog, and Modal's GPU rates climb steeply with chip size from there, which means your GPU selection becomes a cost decision as much as a performance one.

An L4's $0.80, an A100 40GB's $2.10 and an A100 80GB's $2.50, leaving your hourly cost entirely dependent on your GPU choice, which means picking the wrong GPU triples your hourly bill.

If you want the newer GPU, you'll pay more per hour: the H100's $3.95 and the H200's $4.54. An H100's nearly seven times a T4, and one left idle for a day costs $94.80, making GPU waste genuinely expensive.

Between February and August 2024 the H100 went from $7.65 an hour to $4.56, according to Modal's own pricing article, so list prices fall substantially.

It's $3.95 as of October 2026, about half the early price. A budget built on an old quote overstates your cost, so date every figure you use.

results.title: How does Modal pricing work for training and fine-tuning? | Nodus Blog
results.author: Nodus Compute Engineering
highlights:
Modal bills a training run per second across three meters, GPU, CPU cores and memory, and multiplies the sum by 1.15x or 1.75x if you pin a region. Nodus lists the same NVIDIA H100 at $2.60/hr on its pricing page, against $3.95/hr for Modal’s GPU meter alone, and restores your checkpoint when a machine is reclaimed. On Modal, a preempted run that starts over is billed again, so checkpointing is part of the price.

...

## What does Modal charge for while a training job runs?

Modal bills each running container for three things at once. The GPU meter is the big one, and CPU and memory are charged on top of it, per second, at the amounts you request or actually use, whichever is higher.

| Meter | Modal list rate | Per hour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | $0.001097 / sec | $3.9492 |
| NVIDIA B200 | $0.001736 / sec | $6.2496 |
| NVIDIA A100 80 GB | $0.000694 / sec | $2.4984 |
| CPU, per physical core (2 vCPU) | $0.0000131 / sec | $0.04716 |
| Memory, per GiB | $0.00000222 / sec | $0.007992 |
| Volumes | $0.09 per GiB-month, first 1 TiB free | |
| Network egress | $0.04 per GiB beyond the plan’s included amount | |

Prices checked November 6, 2026, from modal.com/pricing. Hourly figures are the per-second rates times 3,600.

Two details on that page are easy to miss. Each container has a minimum request of 0.125 cores and 128 MiB, and you pay for the higher of what you request and what you use. Modal also says it may run a `gpu="H100"` request on an H200, or a `gpu="A100"` request on an 80 GB A100, without changing the price. A `gpu="B200+"` request is billed as B200 even when it lands on a B300 (GPU guide).

...

A single-GPU LoRA fine-tune shows how the meters add up. We priced one H100 for 8 hours with 8 physical cores and 64 GiB of memory, an assumed shape for a 7B to 13B model with a data loader running alongside.

| Line | Arithmetic | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU | $3.9492 x 8 h | $31.59 |
| CPU | 8 cores x $0.04716 x 8 h | $3.02 |
| Memory | 64 GiB x $0.007992 x 8 h | $4.09 |
| Modal total, no region set | | $38.70 |
| Same run pinned to `us` (1.15x) | $38.70 x 1.15 | $44.51 |
| Same run pinned to `us-west` (1.75x) | $38.70 x 1.75 | $67.73 |

results.title: Free GPU hours on Modal: what $30 a month really buys
highlights:
## How many GPU hours $30 buys

Modal's pricing page lists GPU prices per second. Multiply by 3,600 for the hourly rate, then divide $30 by it:

| GPU | GPU memory | Price per hour | Hours for $30 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H200 | 141 GB | $4.54 | 6.6 |
| H100 | 80 GB | $3.95 | 7.6 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 96 GB | $3.03 | 9.9 |
| A100 80 GB | 80 GB | $2.50 | 12.0 |
| A100 40 GB | 40 GB | $2.10 | 14.3 |
| L40S | 48 GB | $1.95 | 15.4 |
| A10 | 24 GB | $1.10 | 27.2 |
| L4 | 24 GB | $0.80 | 37.5 |
| T4 | 16 GB | $0.59 | 50.8 |

Treat these as ceilings. CPU cores and memory are metered alongside the GPU, so a real workload gets a little less. Pinning containers to a region multiplies prices by 1.15 to 1.75, so leave placement to Modal unless you need it. One small bonus: according to Modal's GPU guide, a plain `gpu="H100"` request may run on an H200 at no extra cost.
